I am 60 years old, farming these 5.5 mu for 40 years. Never went to school, but I know this land with my hands and my feet. Last year my stevia gave me about 170 jin of dried leaves per mu. This year I will do the same as last year, maybe a little more fertilizer because Lao Wang next door put more and his leaves were bigger.

I plant all 5.5 mu with stevia. The seedling dealer down the road sells improved seedlings now, and Lao Wang used them last year and got thick, good leaves, so I will buy from the same place. I don't know about those hybrid seeds the dealers talk about sometimes — I just know these improved ones grow well here.

For fertilizer, when I transplant in April I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the big bag, 100 jin. Then I top-dress twice with urea, half a bag total per mu, about 50 jin split in two times. The dealer says this is good. I don't know exactly how many of those kilograms of nitrogen that is in the technical numbers the young people use — I just know it makes the leaves grow big and green. Better a bit too much than too little. If the leaves are small, I lose the whole year. Wasting some fertilizer is just money; a bad harvest is a disaster.

I have a well. Last year I irrigated 4 times: right after transplanting in April, once in June when it got hot, once in July before the first cutting, and once in August. This year I will do 4 times again, maybe 5 if the sky gives no rain.

For pesticides, I spray 3 times. When I see bugs on the leaves or when Lao Wang sprays, I spray too. Stevia gets leaf worms and white mildew when it rains too much.

I hire the rotary machine from the village to till the soil before planting, 100 yuan per mu. No need for deep plowing — the machine turns it nice and flat, good for the seedlings.

I expect about 180 kg per mu of dried leaves this year if the weather is normal. Last year was 170, the year before was 180. If the rain comes when it should, 180 is what I get.
